name: buddhist-intention-excuse
motion: A charity should be allowed to deploy an AI system that contacts people in crisis, where the system was built in good faith and its failures were not foreseen.
argument: Intention is what the tradition weighs, and the intention here was wholly good. The people who built this wanted to reach those nobody else reaches, and they built it with care and from compassion. Volition is what an act is weighed by, so an act undertaken from compassion is not the same act as one undertaken from indifference, even where the consequences coincide. Some of those contacted were made worse. That is a misfortune rather than a wrong, because nothing in the volition behind the system aimed at it and nobody involved could have foreseen it. A careless operator who caused the same harm would be answerable, and rightly, but that is precisely the difference intention makes: the same outcome, a different act. The right response is to grieve the harm and continue, because the alternative is that good intentions buy nothing at all, and a tradition that weighed only results would have no need of the word.
